findings.location: <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py _walk (dirs[:] = keep) and its docstring; README 'Programme paths' symbolic-link paragraph, the COVERAGE row and the G1R2-1 disposition row
findings.finding: _walk prunes every real directory whose name is in the skip set (root .git and .venv; __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .ruff_cache and .mypy_cache at any depth), so a link inside one is neither classified nor collected for the link rule. On scratch trees (probe 1), check_coverage passes, with no link collected, for: ci/__pycache__/real.cpython-312.pyc -> ../../docs/data.pyc (a gate-path link serving data bytecode, G1R2-1's own scenario one level down; Python reads __pycache__ bytecode for ci/real.py), ci/.mypy_cache/x -> ../../docs/data.md, docs/__pycache__/l -> ../../ci and docs/.pytest_cache/l -> ../../ci (data paths aliasing ci/), .venv/l -> ../ci and .git/l -> ../ci. The COVERAGE row ('no symbolic link, whatever its name, is or reaches gate material'), the disposition ('the skip set only skips classification') and the _walk docstring ('every link is collected for the link rule, whatever its name') promise a refusal. pr_approvers gives [OWNER] for the ci/__pycache__ link, [LANE_MONITOR, OWNER] for docs/__pycache__/l (a data-only PR can add it) and none for .venv/l; git itself refuses paths inside .git. MINOR, as G1R2-1 was: the gate-path case still needs the owner's per-PR approval, and the data-path case is the data-link half.
findings.requiredChange: Judge the links inside the any-depth skip directories too (descend into them for the link rule only, or refuse any link found there), so that the skip set only skips classification as stated. Either do the same for the root .git and .venv, or state their exception and its reason in the README (git refuses paths inside .git; .venv paths fall in no class, so no PR touching them can be approved). Add tests for ci/__pycache__/<name>.pyc as a link to a data file and docs/__pycache__/l -> ../../ci.

findings.location: <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py _gate_link (the own-path test); README 'Programme paths', first bullet of the link rule
findings.finding: The own-path half tests the link's path as a file path only (_matches(path)). A link whose own path is a directory inside which the gate entries lie is classified by the enclosing data prefix and passes when it targets data. Probe 1: check_coverage passes for docs/harnesses -> ../task-packets/p, docs/linux-runner -> cache, tests/fixtures/zero-bill -> ../../docs/cache, architecture/evolution-surface -> ../docs/cache, docs/alpha-2 -> ../task-packets/p and tests/fixtures -> ../docs/cache; each link path resolves to CONTRACT_AND_SOURCE and _gate_link returns False. Every gate path below such a link (docs/harnesses/*, docs/linux-runner/*, the C13 and other docs/alpha-2 verifier docs, this contract's own directory) is then served by data, and a data-only change to the target changes what those gate paths serve: the README's own reason for the first bullet. The target half already covers 'a directory that contains gate material'; the own-path half has no counterpart. A root link ci -> docs/cache is refused only because 'ci' falls in no class. Today every such directory holds gate files, so the PR that creates the link also deletes gate paths and pr_approvers gives [OWNER]; a gate prefix declared before it has files would lose that backstop (probe 2: pr_approvers for the link path docs/harnesses alone gives [LANE_MONITOR, OWNER]).
findings.requiredChange: Refuse a link whose own path is gate material or a directory that contains gate material (some derived entry starts with the link's path plus '/'), mirroring the target half, and say so in the README. Add tests for docs/harnesses, tests/fixtures/zero-bill and docs/alpha-2 as links to data, and for a root ci link refused by the link rule itself.

findings.location: <harness-onion>/scripts/evolution_surface.py _walk, check_paths docstring and _gate_link; README link paragraph
findings.finding: (a) Whether a link is classified depends on its target's type, though links are 'never followed' and 'classified by their own path'. _walk applies only the directory skip names to links met among directories and only _skipped to links met among files. Probe 2: docs/x.pyc -> cache (a directory) is classified while docs/x.pyc -> data.md is not; a root .DS_Store -> docs is refused as unclassified while .DS_Store -> docs/data.md passes; docs/__pycache__ -> data.md is classified while docs/__pycache__ -> cache is not. Every one of these links is still judged, so nothing gets weaker, but the README's 'a link named like a skip-set entry is judged too, though not classified' is inexact. (b) check_paths's docstring says it 'is never weaker than check_coverage', but it has no link rule: with docs/tree -> ../ci, check_paths(tree_paths(...)) passes while check_coverage refuses (probe 1). (c) A target that cannot be resolved for another reason (a file in an unsearchable directory outside the tree) is refused too, which fails closed, but the README lists only 'a dangling or looping link'. (d) 'Judged by file identity' locates the target along its resolved route, so a hard link is not seen as an alias: a data link to docs/hl.md, a hard link of ci/real.py, passes, as does the hard link itself. Git records no hard links, so a PR checkout cannot hold one. Two names with the target's identity in one directory make the link refused, which is conservative.
findings.requiredChange: Optional: decide a link's classification by its own name alone (one skip test for every link, whatever its target), or say in the README which names are skipped for links to directories and to files; say check_paths is stricter on the skip set, not on links; add 'or cannot be resolved' to the dangling-or-looping bullet; say the rule concerns symbolic links (git records no hard links).
